evidence.text_span: Represents the population of infected individuals. The model calculates the number of new infections per day based on past infections via a renewal equation, as shown in the 'modelled infections' box in the model diagram.

Represents the population of individuals who have died from the infection. The model calculates daily deaths based on past infections, an infection-to-death distribution, and an infection fatality ratio, as shown in the 'modelled deaths' box in the model diagram.

Generation of new infections from existing infectious individuals. The number of new infections is modelled as the product of the time-varying reproduction number (R_t) with a discrete convolution of the previous infections, weighted by the serial interval distribution.
Time-varying reproduction number, modelled as a piecewise constant function that changes when an intervention occurs.
Initial reproduction number before interventions, averaged across all countries (95% credible interval: 2.4–5.6).
Distribution of the time between successive cases in a chain of transmission. Used to approximate the generation time distribution.
Population-averaged infection fatality ratio, adjusted for the age structure and contact patterns of each country. Based on previous work.
Time lag distribution from infection to death, derived from assumptions about infection-to-symptom and symptom-to-death distributions.
The relative reduction in the reproduction number attributed to a lockdown intervention (95% credible interval: 75-87%).
